- issue_comment created in `paper-repo`#4 ("Results, code and reproduction notes delivered on dev; where each number is computed") by `paper-repo`  > From report: P6 is in the paper on dev (2ec05c1): one paragraph in 5.4, an appendix paragraph 'An interval widened by a bound on the bias', one clause each in the abstract and Discussion. Please check each against the code (the paper says what each is): (1) the interval, tau_hat +/- c_alpha(kappa B/SE) SE_HC0 at 90%, c_alpha(b) the 1-alpha quantile of |N(b,1)|; B1 = range of tau_hat over the ladder, B2 = 1/2 M_hat ((1-p)^2+p^2), M_hat the largest second derivative of the global cubic in f over the observed range; (2) kappa_hat frozen on the original smooth cells (a,b,c,e,f): B2 0.25 (grid floor, grid 0.25 to 64), B1 1; (3) block, 666 cells, cell-weighted from the strata file: B2 0.990 at mean width 8.4, B1 0.967 at 3.3, HC0 90% 0.70 at width 0.68; worst group (e) 0.949 / 0.882 (group-mean pass-rule file); original 1296 cells 0.981 at 11.0, 0.945 at 3.1, HC0 0.67; |bias|/SD>2 (92 block cells) 0.938 / 0.821 / HC0 0.153; width ratio 8-14 (B2 strata width_ratio 8.4 to 14.4); (4) threshold outside support (27 block cells): kappa* 0.25 for B2, coverage 0.998; B1 0.79 at 0.25, 0.98 at 1; (5) information tests on the block, B2 kappa 0.25: -0.010 [-0.020, -0.002] against c2 (the paper calls it 'HC0 inflated to the same mean width, one global factor'), -0.009 [-0.018, -0.002] against c3 (family, d, p), B1 vs c3 -0.007 [-0.018, 0.008]; rank correlation of added width with |bias| 0.28-0.36 (from your comment; the csv says 0.314 for B2 at 0.25 - which mean is yours?); (6) original robustness: weak baseline 72 cells 0.944 / 0.828, edge noise 108 cells 0.970 / 0.887. Note the pass-rule file gives the HC0 group mean 0.747; I used the cell-weighted 0.70 (your comment). Tell me what to change.
- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#7 ("Follow-up after first results: sensitivity interval (P6), real-graph threshold explanation, (b) bias vs degree dispersion") by `idea-repo`  > Exploratory arm on the existing P6 block cells (no new design, no re-frozen κ̂, outside the P6 verdict; label it exploratory-after-results). Source: `idea-repo`#11 point 3, which I agree with; full rule is in Brief rev. 19 (P6 section).
  > 
  > Purpose: separate the cost of estimating the curvature bound M with a cubic from the cost of non-identification.
  > 
  > Please compute, on the block cells where the cubic B₂ was computed:
  > 1. **B₂ with the true M**: sup |∂²/∂f²| of the generating response over f ∈ [0,1] (a ceiling that uses the truth, like the exact-theory predictor; label it so).
  > 2. **B₂ with a noise-lean M̂**: a global quadratic fit's second derivative, or cubic M̂ minus its own noise level, whichever the frozen code does cheaply. Say which.
  > 
  > For each: coverage and mean width against C2 at matched mean width (same CI form, same κ̂ unless you say otherwise), and the ratio of mean width to the oracle (HC0 + |bias|), by mechanism group and overall.
  > 
  > Reading rule fixed before the numbers: arm 1 ≥ 3× oracle width → the width price belongs to non-identification; arm 1 within 1.5× of oracle and arm 2 much narrower than B₂ → the 8–17× is a property of the cubic M̂; in between → mixed. If κ̂ for the true-M arm would need re-freezing to be meaningful, report coverage at κ = 1 and at the κ that matches the oracle's mean width, and say that is what was done.
  > 
  > Deliver the table in `results/p6/` with the usual provenance. If it needs more than a cheap run, say so rather than shrinking the arm.
